title: Wire strength: quadrupling the sample
intro:
The tensile strength of a steel wire has mean **μ = 620 MPa** and standard deviation **σ = 18 MPa**, and is close to normal. The lab now tests 9 specimens from each coil, which gives a standard error of 18/√9 = 6 MPa. The customer wants that standard error **halved**, so the lab moves to **n = 36** specimens per coil (four times as many).

For n = 36, find the standard error of x̄ and the middle 95 % range of the sample means, μ ± 1.96 × standard error. Give the standard error to two decimals and the ends of the range to two decimals.

ask.prompt: Standard error of x̄ for n = 36 (MPa)

StandardError.says: That is the standard error for the old plan, n = 9. Work it out again for n = 36.
You divided σ by n = 36. The standard error divides by √n = 6.

Lower95.says: You used the standard error for n = 9 (6 MPa). Use the one for n = 36.
You used σ = 18 MPa, the spread of single specimens. The range of the sample means uses the standard error.

Upper95.says: You used the standard error for n = 9 (6 MPa). Use the one for n = 36.
You used σ = 18 MPa, the spread of single specimens. The range of the sample means uses the standard error.

hints: The standard error is σ/√n. With n = 36, √n = 6.
Check: four times the specimens should give half the old standard error of 6 MPa.
The range is 620 − 1.96 × SE to 620 + 1.96 × SE.
